items.title: `std::ui::kit::virtual_list`: what the first version leaves out (estimated row extents, its own padding, positions past 4 million dp, a focused row scrolled away)
items.discussion: lane kit-b (Order 58, 2026-11-12); the first version takes a fixed row extent in dp
items.body: (1) ESTIMATED EXTENTS: rows of differing heights need a resize notice per row (the host's `on_resize` is in), a prefix-sum tree over n heights to map an offset to an index, and scroll anchoring when a measured height differs from its estimate; vilan work only, the lane's guess is a day. (2) The list's own padding is not subtracted from the viewport height. (3) Row positions are `f32`: beyond about 4 million dp (125,000 rows of 32 dp) a position loses part of a pixel; positions relative to the window's first row would remove the limit. (4) A focused row the wheel scrolls out of the window is removed and loses the focus; decide whether the focused row is kept built (the web's virtual lists differ here). (5) A deferred reveal does not update the hover until the next pointer move. DECIDED IN LANE, owner may overrule: the extent is a required argument; overscan defaults to 2; Tab builds one row ahead before the focus moves and leaves the list at its real ends; an insert above the window keeps the offset; `reveal` moves as little as needed; the list sets `role(List)` and leaves row roles to the app; `on_resize` and `impl Element with Attributes` are public; the resize-and-layout loop is capped at 8 passes.

items.title: `ListCell::peek` does not build natively (the `WeakGet` intrinsic is missing in the native backend)
items.discussion: found by lane kit-b (Order 58, 2026-11-12); `examples/ui-virtual-list` uses `get()` instead
items.body: Repro: a native build of a program that calls `peek()` on a `ListCell`. Add the intrinsic (or the path `peek` takes to it) with a `native_differential` pin on both backends, then switch the example back to `peek()` where it reads without subscribing.
